steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
1. Electrify urban transportation  
   • Replace diesel buses, taxis, and municipal fleets with electric vehicles.  
   • Expand charging infrastructure and offer incentives for e-bikes, scooters, and EV car-sharing.  
   • Pair with clean grids so tailpipe emissions disappear instead of moving upstream.

2. Retrofit and decarbonize buildings  
   • Mandate high-efficiency insulation, heat pumps, and smart energy-management systems for new and existing structures.  
   • Offer green-loan programs or tax rebates to homeowners and landlords.  
   • Adopt performance standards that phase out fossil-fuel heating and cooking appliances.

3. Expand low-carbon urban planning  
   • Zone for mixed-use, transit-oriented development so people live closer to work, schools, and services.  
   • Invest in rapid transit, protected bike lanes, and pedestrian corridors to cut car dependency.  
   • Preserve and plant urban green spaces, which absorb CO₂ and lower cooling demand.
